title: Delta-profile driven batch advisor for continuous-serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams running low-latency LLM endpoints face high token costs because static batch configurations either leave GPUs underutilized or introduce tail latency. We need an automated recommender that turns live workload telemetry into safe, incremental batching/caching configuration suggestions and can apply them with canaryed rollback when regressions are detected.

Goal: Build a Delta-Profile Driven Batch Advisor that: (1) continuously profiles request patterns per route (open/closed loop, seq len, arrival distribution, KV hit rates), (2) generates heuristic-driven candidate configs for batching/windowing/kv-cache policies, (3) simulates expected cost and p50/p95 latency impact, (4) provides confidence scores and safety fences, and (5) supports automated canary apply + rapid rollback with audit trail.

This ticket covers the core recommender + safe-apply controller and the first production canary flow for a single-region runtime class (n1-gpu). Subsequent tickets will cover multi-region rollout, model-family specific kernels, and console UIs.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender service produces per-route candidate configs hourly and stores deltas in config-store with metadata (confidence, expected cost delta, risk score)

Simulator provides p50/p95 latency and cost delta estimates for each candidate using sampled telemetry (no production injection) with <10% estimation error vs offline ground truth on historical traces
Safe-apply controller can perform a canary apply to 5% of traffic for a chosen route, monitor key metrics (p50, p95, error-rate, token cost), and rollback automatically if thresholds exceeded
All applied changes have immutable audit entries (who/when/why/prev-config) recorded in audit-log and surfaced in the runtime-ops dashboard
E2E test harness validates apply + rollback flow using synthetic replay traffic and failsafe timers
Documentation (PRD + Runbook) is published with rollout guidance and knob descriptions
implementation_notes:
Architecture: 1) profiler-worker consumes aggregated telemetry + per-request samples from hot route shards (windowed: 1h/6h/24h) and emits workload signatures; 2) heuristic-engine translates signatures to candidate batch/cache configs (window sizes, max_tokens_in_batch, continuous-batch alpha/beta, kv-cache expiry and warm-up thresholds); 3) offline-simulator replays sample traces against a cost/latency model to estimate impact; 4) recommender stores candidates with confidence + risk; 5) safe-apply controller executes canary rollout using traffic-split service and monitors SLOs; 6) rollback automations revert config and mark candidate as rejected.

Key heuristics: dynamic windowing tied to inter-arrival CDF; penalize variance spikes; prefer smaller increases for routes with >2% p95 tail sensitivity; require KV warm-up period when recommending aggressive cache TTL increase.

Safety fences: never increase max_tokens_in_batch beyond model-specific kernel breakpoint; cap batch growth to 2x per-apply; require historical p95 headroom >= 10ms before applying aggressive changes.

Data retention: profiler samples stored 14 days, signatures 90 days.

Operational hooks: metrics emitted: advisor.confidence, advisor.expected_cost_delta, advisor.risk_score, advisor.apply_state, advisor.rollback_count. Logs include candidate_id and sample_trace_ids.
tasks: Define workload signature schema and sampling strategy (profiler)
Implement heuristic-engine basic rule set and config schema
Build offline-simulator integrated with token-cost model
Implement recommender API and config-store integration
Safe-apply controller with canary traffic split + rollback watchdog
Add unit + integration tests and e2e replay harness
Add metrics and dashboard panels for advisor results and canary health
Write PRD summary and runtime runbook
risks: Simulator estimation may under-approximate tail latency if sampling bias exists
Aggressive automated applies could increase error rates if safety fences are mis-tuned
Cross-route interference (shared GPU pools) can invalidate per-route predictions; requires pool-awareness
Telemetry volume and storage cost if sampling not rate-limited
telemetry_queries: sql: SELECT route, sequence_length, arrival_ms, kv_hit FROM request_samples WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hours' LIMIT 100000
test_plan: Unit tests for heuristic transformations and config schema validation
Simulator accuracy tests against historical traces (compare predicted vs observed cost/latency)
Integration test: end-to-end candidate generation -> store -> apply -> rollback using local traffic-split shim
E2E replay in staging with synthetic fuzzed inter-arrival distributions to validate safety fences
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout in staging for routes with <100 RPS
Canary apply to 5% of production traffic for selected route for 30m observation window
If no regressions, increase to 25% for 2 hours, then 100% active after manual approve
If auto-rollback triggers, create postmortem draft and mark candidate as rejected with reason codes
Gradual expansion to additional runtime classes after two weeks of stable canaries
monitoring_alerts: Alert if p95 latency increases >10% and error_rate increases >0.5% within canary window
Alert if simulator_estimation_error > 15% on historical validation job

2026-03-05 Design review: Decided to keep UI surface minimal in V1; expose candidate summary + risk score and a single 'apply canary' button.
2026-03-08 Marco Ruiz: Implemented heuristic-engine MVP and unit tests. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Simulator baseline completed; early validation shows <8% cost estimation error on last 7 days of traces for low-variance routes
notes_for_SE: When onboarding customers to early access, collect a 24h request sample and a 1h detailed sample to seed profiler. Recommend starting with conservative canary (2-5%) and make sure customers have ability to pin to previous config quickly via tenant-level override.
